canonical_statement: DECLARE–TIMI 58 was a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multinational cardiovascular outcomes trial.
The trial was conducted at 882 sites in 33 countries.
Participants completed a 4-to-8-week placebo run-in before randomization.
Eligible participants were randomized 1:1 to dapagliflozin or placebo.
The intervention was dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily, added to current background therapy.

exposures.details: Randomized double-blind study treatment added to background therapy.

canonical_statement: The comparator was matching placebo once daily, added to current background therapy.

exposures.details: Randomized matching placebo added to background therapy.

canonical_statement: After randomization, in-person visits occurred every 6 months with telephone contact every 3 months between visits.

Use of other glucose-lowering medications was permitted at the treating physician’s discretion, except open-label SGLT2 inhibitors, pioglitazone, and rosiglitazone were restricted as specified by the protocol.
Participants were required to be at least 40 years old and have type 2 diabetes.
Eligible glycated hemoglobin was at least 6.5% and less than 12.0%.
Creatinine clearance at screening had to be at least 60 mL/min.
Participants qualified through either established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease or multiple cardiovascular risk factors.

canonical_statement: The prespecified renal composite was a sustained decrease in eGFR of at least 40% to below 60 mL/min/1.73 m², new end-stage renal disease, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes.

outcome.definition: Sustained ≥40% eGFR decrease to <60 mL/min/1.73 m², new ESRD, or renal/cardiovascular death

canonical_statement: Death from any cause was a prespecified secondary efficacy outcome.
A prespecified additional renal composite used the renal criteria but excluded cardiovascular death.

canonical_statement: Hospitalization for heart failure was evaluated as an individual component of the cardiovascular-death-or-heart-failure composite.
Primary cardiovascular safety and efficacy analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle using adjudicated events.
Time-to-event hazard ratios were estimated with Cox proportional-hazards models stratified by baseline ASCVD category and baseline hematuria status.
Safety analyses used participants who received at least one dose of dapagliflozin or placebo.
Safety-event P values were reported without adjustment for multiple testing.
Thirty randomized participants from one site were excluded because serious Good Clinical Practice violations in another trial created uncertainty about data integrity.

The original trial design used MACE as the primary efficacy outcome; after external EMPA-REG OUTCOME results, the executive committee added cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure as a second primary efficacy outcome before the DMC reviewed comparative MACE efficacy data.
The two primary efficacy outcomes split the available alpha, and the sample size was not increased after the amendment.
The final Statistical Analysis Plan was Edition 8 dated 31 May 2018.

canonical_statement: The final SAP specified Full Analysis Set, safety analysis set, and on-treatment analysis set definitions before final analysis.
The final SAP specified Cox proportional-hazards, Kaplan–Meier, repeated-measures, proportion, and incidence-rate methods and a closed testing procedure for efficacy variables.
The final SAP prespecified analyses addressing incomplete follow-up and sensitivity analyses for primary variables.

Before alpha recycling, the amendment left approximately 80% power to detect a 20% relative reduction in cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure and approximately 78% power to detect a 15% MACE reduction; recycling could increase MACE power above 85%.

canonical_statement: The revised protocol/SAP was supplied to regulators before the DMC’s first review of MACE efficacy data.
DECLARE–TIMI 58 was initially supported by AstraZeneca and Bristol-Myers Squibb and, by publication, by AstraZeneca alone.
The complete raw database was provided to the TIMI Study Group, which independently conducted the analyses reported in the article.
The article states that a data-sharing statement is available with the full text at NEJM.org.
A total of 17,160 participants were randomized in DECLARE–TIMI 58.
Among randomized participants, 6,974 (40.6%) had established ASCVD and 10,186 (59.4%) had multiple risk factors without established ASCVD.
Participants were followed for a median of 4.2 years (IQR 3.9–4.4), totaling 69,547 patient-years.
Baseline mean HbA1c was 8.3±1.2%.
Median duration of type 2 diabetes was approximately 11 years.
Mean baseline eGFR was approximately 85.2 mL/min/1.73 m², and only about 7% had eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m².
About 10% of randomized participants had a history of heart failure at baseline.
At baseline, approximately 82% used metformin, 41% insulin, 43% sulfonylureas, 17% DPP-4 inhibitors, and 4%–5% GLP-1 receptor agonists.
At baseline, approximately 81% used an ACE inhibitor or ARB, 75% a statin or ezetimibe, 53% a beta-blocker, and 41% a diuretic.
Premature study-drug discontinuation occurred in 21.1% of dapagliflozin participants and 25.1% of placebo participants.
Withdrawal of consent occurred in 224 participants and loss to follow-up in 30 participants.

The placebo run-in screened 25,698 participants before 17,160 were randomized; the supplement documents 52 exclusions from one site related to data-integrity concerns, including 22 during run-in and 30 after randomization.
Average HbA1c was 0.42 percentage points lower with dapagliflozin than placebo during follow-up.

canonical_statement: Table 2 safety P values and confidence intervals were not adjusted for multiple comparisons.

The supplement’s Table S3 lists serious adverse-event preferred terms occurring in more than 0.2% of either treatment arm; these were investigator-reported MedDRA events and not the adjudicated efficacy endpoints.
Dapagliflozin was noninferior to placebo for MACE safety but did not significantly reduce MACE.
Dapagliflozin significantly reduced cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, driven by fewer heart-failure hospitalizations.
The trial provided additional findings supporting a possible lower rate of adverse renal outcomes with dapagliflozin.
No significant reduction in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality was demonstrated.
The co-primary efficacy structure was introduced during the trial in response to external EMPA-REG OUTCOME findings rather than being part of the original design.
Splitting alpha between two primary efficacy outcomes without increasing sample size could have reduced statistical power.
The placebo run-in required adherence and could have selected against participants who would have difficulty adhering in routine practice.
Screening creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min was an exclusion criterion, limiting representation of chronic kidney disease and potentially limiting mortality comparisons.
Because MACE was not significantly reduced, analyses of additional efficacy outcomes outside the successful primary heart-failure composite were described as hypothesis-generating.
Safety comparisons in Table 2 used unadjusted P values and confidence intervals across multiple comparisons.
The randomized population contained relatively few participants with eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² because of the creatinine-clearance eligibility threshold.
